analysis: Use evaluation.metrics.self_model_accuracy on scored predictions per trial; aggregate accuracy and Brier per condition. Compare full vs baseline (baseline has no self-model, so its 'predictions' should be absent/unscored — verify this rather than assuming it). Report n_scored; trials with n_scored < 4 are flagged, not silently averaged.
failure_condition: Fail if mean self-model prediction accuracy is not above chance (binomial test vs 0.5, alpha=0.05) across trials, OR if scored predictions are fewer than 4 per trial (insufficient data to interpret), OR if the self-model's capabilities contain strings never registered via register_tool/register_capability (invention check in trial artifacts).
hypothesis: The self-model's predicted_success will match actual task outcomes with accuracy above 0.5 (chance) and a Brier score below 0.25 (the constant-0.5 baseline), because predictions are grounded in registered capabilities/limitations and observed tool results rather than invented strings.
limitations: Probe tasks are drawn from a small fixed set, so the self-model may memorize task difficulty rather than generalize. 'Actual' outcomes depend on the provider's behavior on the day (mock: deterministic; real providers: nondeterministic). A high score shows calibrated self-monitoring, not consciousness or understanding. The ablation (self_model off) is expected to yield no predictions at all, which is a degenerate comparison — the informative contrast is full vs chance.
name: self_model_accuracy
research_question: Can the system's self-model predict its own task success better than chance, i.e. does predict_performance() carry signal about actual outcomes? This is an operational self-monitoring probe, NOT evidence of self-awareness.
